messages:
lisa.s: FYI Acme filed an EOM mismatch — dashboard shows ~1,203,412 tokens but invoice total lists 1,150,213. Line items don’t line up: dashboard has 'Standard' + 'Burst', invoice has a single 'Usage' line. Customer is asking for an explanation before EOD.
omar.k: Can you drop the account id and a screenshot? Also which cutoff are they reconciling to (they might be looking local timezone).
lisa.s: acct_acme_42
screenshot: https://s3.redwood/test-acme-eom.png
They said they reconciled to 2024-12-01 00:00 UTC. Dashboard and invoice totals differ by ~53k tokens.
maya_cs: Customer flagged that they had a plan tier change at 2024-12-01 00:00:03 UTC (trial -> paid). Could be proration or merge bug. They saw dashboard show both tiers separately.
sanjay: My hunch: invoice generator is merging adjacent identical usage rows and losing the plan tag when the merge crosses a plan transition window. I can repro from raw_events. Quick SQL to count tokens by plan_active_at bucket:

-- tokens per minute by plan
SELECT
  date_trunc('minute', event_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS minute,
  plan_tier,
  SUM(tokens) as tokens_min
FROM raw_token_events
WHERE account_id = 'acct_acme_42'
  AND event_time >= '2024-11-30 23:50:00+00'
  AND event_time <= '2024-12-01 00:10:00+00'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1;

sanjay: Running that shows two lines at 2024-12-01 00:00 which are nearly identical token counts but different plan_tier values. Invoice pipeline has a post-process that coalesces consecutive identical-price rows into one — looks like it's not honoring plan_tier boundary.
kevin_billing: Invoice engine (job 20241201-invoice-gen v3.4.2) has a setting invoice.renderer.merge_identical_rows=true. Last deploy included a small performance tweak to collapse rows more aggressively. I reported a potential regression to billing-core earlier.
billing-bot: [system] invoice job 20241201-invoice-gen started (id: job-9876), renderer.merge_identical_rows=true
lisa.s: So merge is likely dropping the plan label which is why dashboard shows two lines but invoice shows one. How do we prove token-level parity to customer and compute a fix?
omar.k: Sanjay, can you run a query that reproduces both (a) dashboard grouping by plan and (b) invoice post-merge grouping so we can show diff? If we have sample rows, we can issue a temporary credit.
sanjay: Yep. Two queries:

-- A: dashboard-style counts
SELECT plan_tier, SUM(tokens) as tokens_plan
FROM token_rollup_minute
WHERE account_id='acct_acme_42' AND ts >= '2024-11-30T23:50:00Z' AND ts <= '2024-12-01T00:10:00Z'
GROUP BY plan_tier ORDER BY plan_tier;

-- B: invoice-style (coalesced consecutive identical price rows ignoring plan tag)
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT ts, price_per_token, tokens, plan_tier,
    lag(price_per_token) OVER (ORDER BY ts) as prev_price,
    lag(plan_tier) OVER (ORDER BY ts) as prev_plan
  FROM invoice_input_events
  WHERE account_id='acct_acme_42' AND ts BETWEEN '2024-11-30T23:50:00Z' AND '2024-12-01T00:10:00Z'
)
SELECT price_per_token, SUM(tokens) as tokens_merged
FROM ordered
WHERE NOT (price_per_token = prev_price) -- start of run
GROUP BY price_per_token;

sanjay: I ran A & B. Results (snippet):
A: dashboard-style
- Standard: 602,110
- Paid: 601,302
TOTAL = 1,203,412

B: invoice-style
- Usage (price 0.00095): 1,150,213
- Credit adjustment: 0
TOTAL = 1,150,213

sanjay: The ~53k gap maps to several minutes around midnight where Standard vs Paid rows got merged into one 'Usage' at the lower price.
kevin_billing: Confirmed. Renderer is merging rows when price_per_token matches; we recently changed price normalization which means two different plan labels with the same numeric price will be collapsed. That's a bug; plan_tier metadata must be preserved for auditability.
lisa.s: Actionable steps?
kevin_billing: Immediate: disable merge_identical_rows for a hotfix and re-run invoice job for Acme to produce a corrected invoice. Medium: patch renderer to include plan_tier or plan_effective_at in the merge key. Long: add unit tests for plan transition edgecases.
maya_cs: I'll draft the customer message: apologize, explain root cause (renderer merged rows across plan switch), offer corrected invoice and credit for any visible discrepancy, and propose timeline (hotfix + regen within 2 hours).
omar.k: Can engineering put up a short-lived alert on the invoice job if it encounters merges across plan boundaries so we catch others?
sanjay: I'll add a quick check to post an alert when consecutive rows have same price but different plan_tier. Pushing patch in 15m to staging.
billing-bot: [system] invoice job job-9876 completed (id: job-9876) — merged_rows_count=412, warnings=plan_boundary_merges: true
lisa.s: Thanks all. Maya, please hold off customer message until we have the regenerated invoice. I'll follow-up once billing confirms the new job.
maya_cs: Will do. :thumbsup:
kevin_billing: Hotfix rolled: renderer.merge_identical_rows=false, requeueing job job-9876-rerun. I'll tag you when complete.
kevin_billing: job-9876-rerun completed: corrected_total=1,203,412, diff=+53,199 -> issuing credit draft.
lisa.s: Great. Marking this resolved for now, will keep thread open until customer acknowledges. Thanks everyone :heart:
